content: We have carbon NMR data: chemical shifts list. Need number of CH3 groups in the compound. We need to infer structure? Possibly from carbon shifts: typical methyl carbon around 10-30 ppm for aliphatic, but we have 52.24, 43.47, 38.60. Those could be carbons attached to heteroatoms or aromatic? Also aromatic carbons around 120-140 ppm. So likely aromatic ring plus some aliphatic substituents. Need to determine number of methyl groups (CH3). Methyl carbon appears as a signal, but could be overlapping with other aliphatic carbons. We have three aliphatic carbon shifts: 52.24, 43.47, 38.60. Which correspond to maybe O-CH3 (around 55 ppm), N-CH3 (around 40), and maybe CH2? But we need CH3 count. Could be 2 methyl groups (OCH3 and NCH3) and one CH2 (38.6). But CH2 also appears in that region. Need more info. Could use proton NMR to see methyl signals. Let's get proton NMR.
